fichas.title: Airport Functional Areas and Layout
fichas.summary: A schematic airport layout based on Munich airport shows the relationship between runways, parallel and transverse taxiways, apron, terminal, central handling area, air freight, maintenance, administration, services, hotel, and ground transport connections. The drawing is approximately at scale 1:4000; this is a reproduction scale, not a physical dimension. Site plans of Frankfurt am Main airport and Schwerin-Parchim airfield illustrate functional areas and are marked as not for navigational purposes.
uses: Connection to urban rail and road networks

fichas.title: Airfield Categorisation and Airport Design Parameters
fichas.summary: The page describes airport as a general term under Aviation Law, covering airports, airfields, glider airfields, and heliports. Airports and airfields may be transport or special facilities, and may be open to all aviators or serve specific purposes. Airport planning is organized around runway capacity, terminal passenger and freight handling, apron integration, additional operational buildings, service areas, and ground transport connections. The terminal capacity discussion includes connections to main-line trains, urban rail, car parking, and approach roads; check-in, baggage, passport, security, and access controls; waiting-room size; and gate numbers.
